title: SDG 5 性別平等
footer: Teacher Dom · SDG #5 Gender Equality 性別平等

strip.zh: 項全球目標，這是第 5 項

strip.en: your school opened — for girls only
strip.zh: 年，你們學校創校——當時只收女生

strip.en: jobs that are only for boys or only for girls
strip.zh: 種工作只屬於男生或只屬於女生

lines.en: I have been teaching students in Taiwan for a couple of years.
lines.zh: 我在台灣教學生已經有幾年了。
今天的主題：SDG 5 性別平等。

slides.ask_en: Today's question: can a girl or a boy be anything?
slides.ask_zh: 今天的問題：女生和男生，都可以成為任何樣子嗎？

slides.ask_en: In both places, people used to say: “That is not for girls.” Is it still true today?
slides.ask_zh: 這兩個地方，以前的人都說過：「那不是女生做的事。」現在還是這樣嗎？

prompts.en: Stand up if you help with chores at home.
prompts.zh: 在家會幫忙做家事的，站起來。

prompts.en: Stand up if you love sports.
Stand up if you love drawing, singing or dancing.
prompts.zh: 喜歡畫畫、唱歌或跳舞的，站起來。

slides.punch_en: Look around — girls AND boys are standing. Chores and hobbies do not have a gender.
slides.punch_zh: 看看四周——女生和男生都站起來了。家事和興趣，都沒有性別。

slides.body_en: In 2015, every country agreed on 17 Global Goals for 2030. Goal 5 is Gender Equality: girls and boys should have the same chances and the same respect.
slides.body_zh: 2015 年，全世界所有國家訂下 17 項全球目標，要在 2030 年前達成。第 5 項是「性別平等」：女生和男生都應該有一樣的機會、一樣的尊重。

slides.body_en: A stereotype puts people in a box: “Girls can't play soccer.” “Boys don't cry.” But a real person is much bigger than any box.
slides.body_zh: 刻板印象，就是把人裝進框框：「女生不會踢足球。」「男生不能哭。」但是一個真實的人，比任何框框都大得多。

items.en: Girls are bad at math
Women can be pilots
Boys don't cry
Men can be nurses
Pink is only for girls
Girls can play soccer
Cooking is only Mom's job
Boys can dance

slides.note_en: Thumbs up for FACT, thumbs down for STEREOTYPE!
slides.note_zh: 事實比讚，刻板印象比倒讚！

slides.q_en: A boy is hurt, and his father takes him to the hospital. The doctor says: “He is my son!” But the doctor is not his father. Who is the doctor?
slides.q_zh: 一個男孩受傷了，爸爸送他到醫院。醫生說：「他是我兒子！」可是醫生不是他爸爸。醫生是誰？
slides.explain_en: His mother! If that surprised you, a stereotype was hiding in your head.
slides.explain_zh: 是他的媽媽！如果你嚇一跳，表示有個刻板印象躲在你的腦袋裡。

slides.q_en: Your school opened in 1933. Who could study here back then?
slides.q_zh: 你們學校在 1933 年創校。那時候，誰可以在這裡上學？
slides.explain_en: Only girls! Your school began as Yuanlin Girls' School. Back then, many girls in Taiwan never went to school at all.
slides.explain_zh: 只有女生！你們學校一開始叫「員林女子公學校」。那個年代，台灣很多女孩根本沒有機會上學。

slides.ask_en: This is your school! In 1933, only girls studied here. Today, girls and boys learn here together.
slides.ask_zh: 這是你們的學校！1933 年，這裡只收女生。現在，女生和男生一起在這裡學習。

slides.head_en: girls around the world are not in school
slides.head_zh: 全世界大約有 1 億 2,000 萬個女孩沒有上學
slides.body_en: Some must work at home. Some are told that school is not for girls.
slides.body_zh: 有的必須在家工作，有的被告知「女生不用念書」。
slides.ask_en: What would you miss if you could not come to school?
slides.ask_zh: 如果你不能來上學，你會想念什麼？

slides.q_en: She spoke up for girls' right to go to school. At 17, she won the Nobel Peace Prize. Who is she?
slides.q_zh: 她站出來，為女孩爭取上學的權利；17 歲時，她得到諾貝爾和平獎。她是誰？
slides.explain_en: Malala, from Pakistan. “One child, one teacher, one book and one pen can change the world.”
slides.explain_zh: 來自巴基斯坦的馬拉拉。「一個孩子、一位老師、一本書、一支筆，就能改變世界。」

slides.head_zh: 在育英，每個人都能發光
slides.body_en: Yuying has four dance classes — dancing is for anyone who loves it. And a team of Yuying 4th and 5th graders built a chain-reaction machine and won third place at the 2025 World GreenMech Contest in Changhua.
slides.body_zh: 育英有 4 班舞蹈班——跳舞屬於每一個喜歡跳舞的人。育英的四、五年級學生組隊做出連鎖反應機關，拿下 2025 世界機關王競賽彰化縣賽第三名。

slides.head_zh: 真的還假的？手比 ⭕ 或 ❌

items.en: Gender equality is only about girls.
items.zh: 性別平等只跟女生有關。
items.note_en: Boys get put in boxes too — like “boys don't cry.”
items.note_zh: 男生也會被裝進框框——像是「男生不能哭」。

items.en: A girl can be an engineer, and a boy can be a nurse.
items.zh: 女生可以當工程師，男生可以當護理師。
items.note_en: Any job can be done by anyone who learns it.
items.note_zh: 任何工作，只要學會了，誰都可以做。

items.en: Housework is a job for everyone in the family.
items.zh: 家事是家裡每個人的工作。
items.note_en: Yet around the world, women still do about 2.5 times more housework than men.
items.note_zh: 但在全世界，女性做的家事還是大約男性的 2.5 倍。

items.en: Laughing at a boy for being “like a girl” is just a joke.
items.zh: 笑一個男生「像女生」，只是開玩笑。
items.note_en: It tells everyone that being a girl is something bad.
items.note_zh: 這等於告訴大家：當女生是一件不好的事。

slides.body_en: Kuo Hsing-chun lifted weights and won an Olympic gold medal for Taiwan in Tokyo 2020. Tai Tzu-ying was the world's No. 1 badminton player for more than 200 weeks.
slides.body_zh: 郭婞淳在 2020 東京奧運為台灣拿下舉重金牌。戴資穎當了世界球后超過 200 週。

items.en: Anyone can do that.
That's a stereotype.
Boys can cry. Girls can lead.
items.zh: 男生可以哭，女生可以領導。

items.en: Don't put me in a box.
Come and play with us!

slides.rule_en: In 30 seconds, shout out as many JOBS in English as you can. I will count!
slides.rule_zh: 30 秒內，用英文喊出越多「工作」越好，我來數！
slides.target_en: Then tell me: which of these is only for men? (None!)
slides.target_zh: 然後告訴我：哪一個只有男生能做？（一個都沒有！）

slides.prompt_en: What do you love to do? Has anyone ever said it is “only for boys” or “only for girls”?
slides.prompt_zh: 你喜歡做什麼？有沒有人說過那是「男生才能做」或「女生才能做」的？
slides.sentence_en: I love ______. It is for everyone!
slides.sentence_zh: 我喜歡 ______。每個人都可以做！
slides.time_en: 60 seconds — then 3 pairs share with the class.
slides.time_zh: 60 秒，然後請 3 組跟全班分享。

slides.sub_en: Vote with your hands — 1, 2, 3, or 4 fingers.

items.en: Help with the housework at home
Don't laugh at “like a girl” jokes
items.zh: 不跟著笑「像女生」的玩笑

items.en: Let everyone join the game
items.zh: 讓每個人都能加入遊戲

items.en: Cheer for girls' and boys' teams the same
items.zh: 女生隊和男生隊，一樣大聲加油

slides.reveal_en: All four work. #2 is the hardest and the most powerful — it changes what the whole class thinks is okay.
slides.reveal_zh: 四個都有效。第 2 個最難也最有力量——它會改變全班認為「可以接受」的界線。

slides.note_en: Watch — then tell me one stereotype you saw in the video.
slides.note_zh: 看完之後，告訴我你在影片裡看到的一個刻板印象。

slides.head_en: 3 Things You Can Do This Week
slides.head_zh: 這週你可以做的 3 件事

items.en: Do one chore at home that you never do.
items.zh: 在家做一件你從來不做的家事。

items.en: When you hear “that's not for girls” — or boys — say: “Anyone can do that.”
items.zh: 聽到「那不是女生（或男生）做的」，就說：「誰都可以做。」

items.en: Invite someone new to play with you.
items.zh: 邀請一個新朋友跟你一起玩。

slides.q_en: In 1893, which country became the first to let women vote?
slides.q_zh: 1893 年，哪一個國家最先讓女性投票？
slides.explain_en: New Zealand! Women in the U.S. waited until 1920, and in France until 1944.
slides.explain_zh: 紐西蘭！美國女性等到 1920 年，法國等到 1944 年。

slides.body_en: Go to our School Tour page and find the Yuying Elementary column. No sign-up, no login — just write your comment for Teacher Dom.
slides.body_zh: 到我們網站的 School Tour 頁面，找到育英國小那一欄，免註冊、免登入，直接留言跟 Teacher Dom 互動。

slides.big_zh: 每個人，都可以成為任何樣子。
